name: The verb's shape
rule: Some words decide the shape of the verb after them.
After can, will, must, should: the plain verb (can swim).
After enjoy, keep, stop, avoid: the -ing form (enjoy swimming).

wrong.text: My brother enjoys build model planes.

right.text: My brother enjoys building model planes.

spot: Look at the word just before the verb. Does it call for plain, 'to', or -ing?
deeper: After 'to' the verb stays plain: to eat, to play.
Two verbs joined by 'and' or 'or' take the same shape: washing and drying.
After words like 'for', 'by' and 'without', use -ing: by working hard.
